text:
anya: fyi ran into dup billing events during a large partition rebalance. seems similar to previous dup issues but with different failure chain. small log below.

raf: paste the minimal repro and whether this is credits or usage-events?

anya: usage-events (not token credits) — but same consequence. repro: 1) start consumer A on p7 2) emit events 3) trigger rebalance so B claims p7 4) B starts consuming, A still flushing buffered aggregates 5) A crash mid-flush -> both A and B emit overlapping windows. logs: 
```
2026-02-20T09:14:01Z INFO agg.flush start window{42..84}
2026-02-20T09:14:02Z WARN consumer.shutdown unexpected SIGKILL
2026-02-20T09:14:03Z INFO consumer.startup resume at offset 42
2026-02-20T09:14:04Z INFO events.emit window{42..84} sent to billing-sink
```

kevin: sounds like two orthogonal levers: make handoff atomic (manifest/CAS, coordinator-backed commit) OR make sink idempotent (dedupe by (partition, window-epoch)). both are valid. we should think in terms of defense-in-depth.

tara_ops: ops perspective: idempotent sink is nice (simpler handoffs) but it forces us to store dedupe keys in the billing DB index which grows. manifest/CAS adds control-plane complexity and operational hops.

raf: idea: hybrid but with lightweight vector epoching. each partition carries a monotonic epoch vector {partition_epoch, instance_epoch}. Producers tag aggregates with instance_epoch they observed when they started the window. When a consumer wins a handoff, it increments partition_epoch. The sink dedupes based on (partition_id, partition_epoch, window_start). If an old instance emits with stale partition_epoch, sink rejects.

anya: that reduces index size: we dedupe by partition_epoch+window_start only for recent epochs. but we still need a canonical way to advance partition_epoch safely. we can use a compacted KV manifest to CAS the partition_epoch increment.

kevin: to limit scan/backfill costs, make sink accept a small leeway: if it sees a stale epoch within T minutes, it asks for an idempotency proof (event checksum + source-instance) and we run reconciliation; beyond T we treat it as a new legitimate emit. this lets us set retention windows and bound index size.

raf: edge case: what if two consumers both think they incremented epoch concurrently? CAS on manifest prevents double increment if we perform read->CAS with expected epoch. if CAS fails the loser reads new epoch and should abort old-window emissions. but we must ensure consumer doesn't emit before CAS completes. so handoff protocol: 1) acquiring consumer obtains lease, 2) performs CAS(++epoch) on manifest, 3) only after CAS success it starts emitting. old owner must flush and stop emitting before relinquish.

tara_ops: hmm that means we still have a window where old owner could crash after step 1 but before noticing new epoch; the sink will reject based on epoch which is good. need to ensure sink returns a clear error code for "stale-epoch" so the emitter can route to reconcile queue instead of retrying.

kevin: implement a lightweight reconcile queue (topic) for stale-epoch rejects. reconciler validates checksum and either marks event as duplicate or applies compensation. reconciliation should be rate-limited and bounded by retention.

anya: quick perf/ops asks: 1) how expensive is CAS on the compacted KV (p99)? 2) what's expected added metadata size on each emit? 3) recon throughput we need to provision? raf/kevin can you spike numbers?

raf: i'll benchmark CAS latencies on current KV (p99 ~ 15ms intra-region, ~90ms cross-region). if p99 > 50ms for cross-region we should prefer async handoff confirmation and keep the fast path intra-region.

kevin: metadata: partition_epoch + instance_id + window_start ~ 48 bytes per event header. recon queue traffic should be very low (only mis-hands), estimate 0.01% of events. will model in RFC.

recon-bot: created issue PLAT-1128: "epoched-handoff + sink-dedupe spike" and assigned to raf, kevin, anya.

anya: ok action items: raf spike CAS/perf (staging), kevin draft sink-dedupe prototype + stale-epoch error spec, tara_ops draft retention/ops-guardrails (T minutes & recon SLAs). I'll compile into a short RFC next week. thanks :clap:
